Welcome to Voat! I'm not sure which of the three statements you're asking about, so I'll answer them all:

  • less people: Though I hope this doesn't change all at once, this is something that will steadily increase. I encourage you to post lots of stuff you like here because that will definitely improve it!
  • a lot of people who hate Reddit: Erm. It's just the cool thing to do now, in my opinion. I don't hate Reddit at all; I see them as a worthy competitor and something we should eventually challenge as a rival. John Oliver demolishes NCAA rules that prohibit paying student athletes

My feelings are similar, and I absolutely hate the "entitlement" argument. Was the "greatest generation" who came back from WWII entitled? Because they demanded actually pay for play. I know some of them actually went on strike for higher pay to play.

In fact, it was likely these "strikes" for higher wages for CFB players that essentially led to the colleges forming the NCAA to act as a proxy to collude on player compensation. No where else in this country is this type of thing allowed. This is why the NCAA is so adamant that the kids are not "employees." However, if you look at DOL definitions of employees, I do not understand how the players could be defined as anything but employees.

That was the actual ruling by the NLRB on the Northwestern situation. I am not sure why that never moved forward, except that maybe the athletes essentially have no reason to pursue the matter over the duration of a long drawn out case since they will not be at the schools for long enough to benefit from a win.

This pisses me off more than most things do because I wanted to play college sports, but I would have actually had to take a reduction in scholarships, and essentially sign away my rights to many other forms of making income if I did so, so I passed on it. Can you tell I am still bitter?
